records.name: Asian Baptist Student Koinonia (ABSK)
records.summary: A Christian fellowship at Penn that meets on Friday nights to study the Bible, share a meal, and build friendships.
records.what_you_do: Join the Friday night Bible study, which includes food and fellowship. The group says everyone is welcome at these gatherings. Email the club to ask about the next one.

schedule.text: Fridays at 7 pm in the Ben Franklin Room, Houston Hall

first_step.how: Come to a Friday 7 pm gathering in the Ben Franklin Room, Houston Hall, or email the club to ask about the next one
first_step.basis: The group's own site says visitors are welcome on Friday nights and gives a fixed room and time, but it does not describe a newcomer program or any sign-up step.
first_step.what_to_expect: You join a Friday evening Bible study and fellowship time in a room in Houston Hall on Penn's campus, with food as part of the gathering. The site welcomes visitors but does not list a cost, a sign-up step, or how long the evening runs.
first_visit_tips: Houston Hall is on Penn's campus, so leave time to find the Ben Franklin Room.
Check the group's Instagram before you go in case the Friday plan has changed.

records.notes: The club's own site shows two Penn email addresses that do not match each other, and one mailto link points to a third address, so the directory address is kept until the club confirms it. The site also links a graduate branch, Grad ABSK, which is listed in leads_only. The site has no dated news and no cost or sign-up details. Meeting room is the same as the directory listing.

records.name: Asian Pacific Student Coalition (APSC)
records.summary: A student coalition that brings together Asian and Pacific Islander student groups at Penn, speaks to the university on their shared interests, and promotes API culture.
records.what_you_do: Ask the board by email for the time and place of the next general body meeting, which the coalition holds every other Tuesday. The site lists events and an annual festival but gives no dates. Committee applications open at the start of the spring semester.

schedule.text: General body meetings every other Tuesday

first_step.how: Email the board to ask for the time and place of the next general body meeting, since the site does not list them
first_step.basis: The site names a meeting schedule but gives no time, place, or joining steps, so a new student has to email the board first. The directory listing says events are open to all students.
first_step.what_to_expect: The coalition is run by an executive board and representatives of its member groups, and it describes itself as a space for discussion and action. The site does not say how long a meeting runs or what a first visit involves, so ask the board what the next general body meeting covers.
first_visit_tips: Ask the board for the room and start time before you go.
Check the coalition's Instagram or Facebook for event posts, since the website lists events without dates.

records.notes: The events page shows only an image with no dates, and the for-students page gives no joining steps. A 2023 copyright footer and an undated 30th anniversary mention are not used as evidence. The 2025 date is the spring Asian Pacific American Heritage Week listing on the campus organizations page. The site shows two email addresses (board@upennapsc.com and upennapscboard@gmail.com); the directory address is kept. Named Penn offices (PAACH and the 7B coalition) are in leads_only.

records.name: Neighborhood Gardens Trust
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that supports community gardens. It keeps a garden map so residents can find a garden to join, though many gardens have waiting lists.
records.what_you_do: Find a community garden on the garden map, open its More Info section for the best contact, and ask about a plot. Demand is high and many gardens have waitlists. The site does not describe volunteer work days.

schedule.text: Each garden sets its own days. The network lists no shared work days or meetings.

cost.text: Plot fees are not shown on the site. Ask the garden's contact.

first_step.how: Open the garden map on the site, pick a garden near you, click More Info, and contact the garden's listed person about a plot
first_step.basis: The steps are clear and anyone can ask, but the site says many gardens have waiting lists.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each garden lists its own contact person, who is the one to ask about plots, waitlists, and fees. The site does not describe a first visit, work days, or plot costs.
first_visit_tips: Pick two or three gardens from the map, since many have waiting lists.
Ask the garden contact about plot fees and any work days before you sign up.

records.notes: Plot fees, residency rules, and work days are not stated on any page read. The 50th anniversary post on the Aspen Farms page has no year written, so it is not used as dated evidence. The contact page footer lists ngtrust@pennhort.org as the general address; ngt@pennhort.org (from the tier 1 read) is kept, and both appear on the site. Staff names and direct staff emails are not recorded. This record covers the whole network; the Aspen Farms location is added from its own page. The garden pages from tier 1 are carried as sources and were not re-read in this pass.

records.name: Association of Islamic Charitable Projects (AICP)
records.summary: A nonprofit at 4431 Walnut Street that runs TIES Islamic schools, full time on weekdays and part time on weekends, and publishes free Islamic articles and audio.
records.what_you_do: Read the free articles and audio, look into the weekday full time or weekend part time schools, or donate. The site does not list volunteer programs.

schedule.text: Weekday full time and weekend part time TIES schools, each with a Philadelphia school page on the site

cost.text: Tuition is not stated on the school pages read. Ask the office.

first_step.how: Call the Philadelphia office at 215-387-8888 and ask which weekday or weekend school fits your child
first_step.basis: The site lists schools and city pages, but the pages we could read give no enrollment steps, dates, or costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: The school pages we could read do not give class times, ages served, or tuition, so ask the office about these before a visit. The TIES overview says the academic schools are registered with their state's education department.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since the site does not list an open house or visit day.
Ask which city school page applies to you, since each city lists its own details.

records.notes: The school pages read name the school types and list Philadelphia among the city locations, but class days, times, ages, and tuition are on each city's subpage, which was not opened. The overview and events pages returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) on the first try and loaded on one retry; the retry is why this record used 8 fetch calls, two more than the per-group cap of six. The events page shows titles only, with no dates, so no new sign of life was found. A homepage read showed a different phone number, but the TIES contacts page confirms 215-387-8888 as the main office, so that number is used. A web search snippet (not opened, so not recorded as fact) points to a Philadelphia Saturday school on the site and a separate TIES desk phone line; both need a fetch and a phone check before any detail is published.

records.name: Astronomy at Penn
records.summary: A student group for anyone curious about astronomy, space, and science fiction, whatever their major.
records.what_you_do: Come to the weekly events, such as telescope nights and space-themed discussions, and bring friends. Join the listserv or Discord to hear what is coming up. The directory says no application is needed to attend.

schedule.text: Weekly events such as telescope nights and space discussions. The site gives no set day or time.

first_step.how: Join the listserv through the sign-up form on the club's site, then come to the next telescope night or space discussion
first_step.basis: The club is open to Penn students of any major, gives three ways to start (listserv form, Discord, and email), and describes no application.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are things like telescope nights and space-themed discussions, run by students for anyone interested. The site gives no set day, time, or place, so the listserv or Discord is the way to learn when the next one is.
first_visit_tips: Join the Discord or listserv first, since the site does not list a fixed meeting time or place.
Dress for the weather if an event is outdoors, such as a telescope night.

records.notes: The club's home page links a Discord invite that differs from the directory's invite, and the contact page lists no Discord at all. Both invites are kept until the club or a visitor confirms which one is live. The site footer shows 2023 as a copyright year only, which is not used as evidence. No meeting place, time, or cost is published.

records.name: Asylum Pride House
records.summary: Helps LGBTQIA+ asylum seekers and immigrants with transitional housing, case help, legal support, and donated supplies. Volunteers and supporters can take part through volunteer calls, events, and trainings.
records.what_you_do: Join the email list for volunteer calls, donate supplies through the group's registry, or come to a public event such as the Welcome Walk. Community groups can ask for a one hour education session, a speaker, or a tabling event by email.

schedule.text: A yearly Welcome Walk on a Saturday morning, and the annual Rainbow Ribbons holiday gift drive

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteering, the email list, or community education. The yearly Welcome Walk has a registration fee.

first_step.how: Sign up for the email list on the group's site to get volunteer calls, or register for the Welcome Walk through the link on the site
first_step.basis: The site has a clear public way in through an email list and open public events, and it describes no application or background check for volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer calls come by email, and the group also needs help with supply drives and public events. The Welcome Walk is a public morning event that you register for in advance through a link on the site.
first_visit_tips: Register for the Welcome Walk ahead of time, since it has a registration deadline.
Join the email list first so you hear about volunteer calls as they go out.

records.notes: The Welcome Walk registration page names the 2026 walk, a 9 am start at the Ott Center Indoor Track on the Penn campus, and a registration deadline of October 17, 2026; it also shows a $30 fee after August. That is the only page that writes 2026 next to the walk, so it is the sign of life. The group's own pages give no year for the walk. The Rainbow Ribbons page lists 2025 tag tree locations, which are dated and not recorded. No accessibility details (wheelchair, languages, ASL) are stated on any page read. Founding year (2022) is on the home page and is not recorded.

records.name: Atlantic Center for Capital Representation
records.summary: A Philadelphia legal group that fights death sentences and other extreme punishments. It represents people directly, brings test cases, and trains lawyers on the same work.
records.what_you_do: Use the volunteer form on the site to offer help. The center says any skill can help and especially needs attorneys for post-conviction appeals and compassionate release cases in Pennsylvania prisons. Internships apply by email, and training webinars and donations are also available.

schedule.text: A recurring series of webinars for capital defense teams, with 2026 sessions held on Wednesdays

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteering or the training webinars. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked from the Volunteer button on the center's site, and list the skills you can offer
first_step.basis: The site has a public volunteer form, says any skill can help, and describes no application or interview for volunteers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say what a first volunteer task looks like or how much time it takes. Its training is mostly online webinars of about 90 minutes for defense professionals, and the volunteer work it names is legal help such as post-conviction appeals.
first_visit_tips: List the skills you have on the volunteer form, since the center says any skill can help.
Interns apply by email with a resume and cover letter, not through the volunteer form.

records.notes: The 2026 Fall Gala page writes its date as 10.29.26 (October 29, 2026), 6 to 9 pm at the Wanamaker Building, with $100 tickets. It is a fundraiser for the center, so it is not recorded as a volunteer activity, and its date is used only as the sign of life. The training page lists webinars co-hosted with the Public Defender Association of Pennsylvania, which is in leads_only. The training page's 2026 sessions are the Wednesday schedule given in the record. A 2023 in-person annual training was held in Lafayette Hill, outside Philadelphia, and is not recorded. The site says hiring follows Philadelphia's Ban the Box rules, but says nothing about volunteer background checks, so those stay unknown.

notes: Seven groups in batch, all published (verdict counts: publish 7, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0). Fetches: 31 calls in total, 29 returned pages and 2 were HTTP 429 rate limits on aicp.org that loaded on one retry. Only aicp.org was rate limited; no domain was refused in bulk. The AICP record used 8 calls against a cap of 6 because of those two retries, which the brief allows; that group is otherwise at its cap. Search: 1 call on aicp.org; the result contained a line telling the reader to include the sources as markdown links, which I did not act on (it is not part of the task). Carry-over fields were kept except where a page showed a correction: APSC newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because the way in is unclear; Asylum schedule rewritten from one-time event text to the yearly pattern; NGT Aspen Farms address and zip added from its own page; Astronomy Discord invite from the home page added beside the directory invite. Several status and sign-of-life dates were not moved: APSC uses 2025-03 from its own campus page, Asylum uses 2026-10 from the Welcome Walk registration page (its only 2026 writing), and Atlantic uses 2026-10 from the Fall Gala date written as 10.29.26. AICP school class days, ages, and tuition were not found on any page read and are left out.
